scope: Host fixture-helper and admission checks plus cross-compilation only; no native execution or security validation rerun.
findings: Fixed class/stage/status/call/time/health metadata replaces loss of transport failure detail. Raw errors, URLs, headers, bodies and certificate values are never serialized.
Nested timeout classification must walk wrappers because an outer URL error can report false while an inner error times out; focused helper tests cover the repair.
One completion timestamp prevents inconsistent duration/health-age arithmetic. Unique atomic call IDs and one-shot completion are checked with concurrent fake calls under the host race detector.
Strict admission correlates 41 named HTTP outcomes, 10 workload calls and readiness probes with the existing path/load expectations. The raw-prefix case retains its original separate assertions.

Partial diagnostic observations remain available when Go or the supervisor fails; no diagnostic can convert that failure into successful composition. Historical logs without the namespace remain incomplete, never backfilled.
limitations: Only fake transports/synthetic errors and structural receipt mutations were executed. No listeners or network calls in the focused helper tests. The full traffic/security suite and new native diagnostic integration remain unexecuted.

Sampled persistent-health count/age is not an atomic pair or relayd table-state witness; instrumentation may perturb timing. Error classes do not prove a precise failure layer or retroactively diagnose the old native failure.

This is fixture tooling, not a product logging/audit API, runtime repair or qualification of OpenBSD behavior, framing/CRS/resource/architecture adoption. No live service/network/installer/release changes.
Affected security validation remains paused pending clarification of the reported access notice. Ordinary engineering does not grant broader access or bypass safeguards.
